sections.title: Abstract
sections.originalMarkdown: Erasure codes (EC) have been widely adopted to provide high data reliability with low storage costs in clusters. Due to the deletion and out-of-place update operations, some data blocks are invalid, which unfortunately arouses the tedious garbage collection (GC) problem. Several limitations still plague existing designs: substantial network traffic, unbalanced traffic load, and low read/write performance after GC. This paper proposes FastGC, a fast garbage collection method that merges the old stripes into a new stripe and reclaims invalid blocks. FastGC quickly generates an efficient merge solution by stripe grouping and bit sequences operations to minimize network traffic and maintains data block distributions of the same stripe to ensure read performance. It carefully allocates the storage space for new stripes during merging to eliminate the discontinuous free spaces that affect write performance. Furthermore, to accelerate the parity updates after merging, FastGC greedily schedules the transmission links for multi-stripe updates to balance the traffic load across nodes and adopts a maximum flow algorithm to saturate the bandwidth utilization. Comprehensive evaluation results show via simulations and Alibaba ECS experiments that FastGC can significantly reduce 10.36%-81.22% of the network traffic and 34.25%-72.36% of the GC time while maintaining read/write performance after GC.

sections.title: I. INTRODUCTION
sections.originalMarkdown:
Erasure codes (EC) have been widely used in modern massive storage clusters, including Azure [1] and HDFS [2], to maintain high data reliability against frequent failures. Compared to replication [3], it can ensure the same data durability at extremely low storage overhead. Among various erasure codes, Reed-Solomon (RS) codes [4] are the most classic and popular coding construction in production [5]. It takes k fixed-size data blocks as input and encodes m the same fixed-size parity blocks as output via a linear combination, where k + m blocks are stored in k + m nodes and form a stripe [6]. Due to its storage efficiency, RS codes have been widely studied in data repair [7], [8] and update [9], [10].

Deploying the EC in storage clusters causes the tedious garbage collection (GC). The reason is that (i) The intensive workloads in clusters result in frequent deletion operations, and the deleted data will be marked as invalid [11]. For example, the deleted objects account for 26.5% of the total consumed storage capacity for Microsoft OneDrive [12]. (ii) Some storage systems adopt out-of-place updates to avoid the update [13], [14]. Some storage systems writes the updated data into new storage space without rewriting the original data, and the old data becomes invalid. With the increase of invalid data, storage clusters must periodically invoke GC to recycle these invalid data and ensure storage efficiency [15].

However, achieving efficient garbage collection in erasure-coded clusters is challenging. The data blocks are organized into stripes in erasure-coded clusters, and we cannot directly delete invalid blocks as we do in replication-based clusters to guarantee the redundancy of remaining valid data blocks in the same stripe. We analyze the existing works and observe some problems that are not properly addressed.

**High network traffic and imbalanced traffic load.** A common way for GC is to accordingly collect valid data blocks of each stripe and re-encode them into new stripes. For example, GOOD [13] adopts the out-of-place update method and re-encodes the valid data blocks in the stripe with a larger number of invalid blocks. However, re-encoding a new stripe requires reading k valid data blocks and generating m parity blocks, which amplifies the inter-node network traffic by a factor of k + m. In addition, the node responsible for encoding needs to collect data blocks and distribute parity blocks. As a result, the traffic load on this node is heavier compared to other data and parity nodes, which further leads to an imbalance in the traffic load among nodes. The prior study BCStore [16] is proposed to reduce the disk I/O and network traffic during GC. Its main idea is to migrate the valid data blocks from the stripes with the most invalid blocks to the stripes with the least invalid blocks to achieve the least moved blocks (e.g., minimum disk I/O). However, the block migrations that have not been carefully considered and the parity updates of the stripes with the least invalid blocks may unintentionally introduce network traffic during GC. Moreover, data migration causes invalid data of multiple stripes to be rewritten, which can be considered as an update to invalid data, so BCStore must simultaneously manipulate the parity updates of multiple stripes. It does not explicitly design a multi-stripe update method and randomly schedules the transmission routing, which will lead to unbalanced network traffic and hence increase the GC time. The high network traffic and imbalanced traffic load during GC will increase the GC time, thereby degrading service performance.

**Low data read and write performance.** The existing work focuses on reducing the GC cost (e.g., disk I/O and network traffic) during GC, but ignores the impact of the block layout on the data reading and writing performance after GC. For the data read performance, migrated valid data blocks that belong to the same stripe may concentrate on a few nodes, which may cause a degradation in read performance during parallel file access. For example, random data migration in BCStore may move the remaining valid data blocks in the same stripe to the same node. Thus, parallel read operations between different nodes in the original stripe will become sequential read operations within the same node in the new stripe. For the data write performance, the recycling of some stripes will release storage space, which may introduce discontinuous free spaces (called fragments). When writing new data, the discontinuous free space causes a write performance degradation because of frequent disk seeks. Unfortunately, we find none of the existing GC techniques (e.g., GOOD and BCStore) takes into account the fragment problem after GC, and this oversight loses the potential write performance gains in practical storage clusters. Random block migration and discontinuous free spaces may decrease read/write performance after GC, which has a non-negligible impact on the service process.

Therefore, how to achieve a fast garbage collection during GC and maintain fast storage services after GC simultaneously remains an unexplored yet non-trivial issue.

Nevertheless, we observe that stripes with different numbers of valid data blocks exist in erasure-coded clusters. We refer to stripes with fewer than k valid data blocks as non-full stripes; otherwise, they are called full stripes. Therefore, our insight is to select two non-full stripes and merge them into a new full stripe. If the layout of invalid data blocks in one non-full stripe is the same as that of valid data blocks in another, we can generate the new full stripe locally with less network traffic. By doing so, the storage space of one non-full stripe can be recycled, and the data blocks are migrated at the granularity of stripes with a parallel read performance guarantee. Afterwards, two open questions are how to find the merge solution to reduce the network traffic and how to schedule the transmission links to balance the traffic load (e.g., the amount of traffic sent or received by a node) across nodes.

This paper presents FastGC, a Fast Garbage Collection method for RS codes that aims to alleviate network resource consumption and maintain system performance in erasure-coded storage clusters. We make the following contributions:

- We are the first to systematically address the garbage collection problem in erasure-coded clusters and additionally consider balancing the network traffic during GC and maintaining the read and write performance after GC. We exploit the stripe merging idea to recycle the stripes with invalid data blocks and identify the open issues not addressed by existing studies. (Sec. III)
- We propose FastGC, which accelerates garbage collection for RS codes. FastGC first quickly generates the merge solutions by stripe grouping and bit sequences operations to reduce network traffic efficiently. It then carefully allocates the storage space for new stripes during merging to eliminate the discontinuous fragments that affect write performance. Finally, FastGC greedily schedules the transmission links for parity updates to balance the traffic load across nodes and adopts a maximum flow algorithm to saturate the bandwidth utilization. (Sec. IV)
- We implement a FastGC prototype and comprehensively evaluate it by conducting simulations and Alibaba ECS experiments under real-world traces. Evaluations show that FastGC can reduce 10.36%-81.22% of the network traffic and 34.25%-72.36% of the GC time. In addition, we also demonstrate that FastGC effectively balances the inter-node network traffic while maintaining the read/write performance after GC. (Sec. V and VI)

纠删码（EC）已广泛用于 Azure [1] 和 HDFS [2] 等现代大规模存储集群，以在频繁发生故障时维持较高的数据可靠性。与多副本 [3] 相比，它能以极低的存储开销保证相同的数据持久性。在各类纠删码中，Reed-Solomon（RS）码 [4] 是生产环境中最经典、最常用的编码构造 [5]。它以 k 个固定大小的数据块为输入，通过线性组合编码出 m 个同样大小的校验块；这 k + m 个块存放在 k + m 个节点上，构成一个条带 [6]。由于存储效率高，RS 码在数据修复 [7], [8] 和更新 [9], [10] 方面得到了广泛研究。

在存储集群中部署 EC 会带来棘手的垃圾回收（GC）问题。原因有二：（i）集群中的密集负载导致频繁的删除操作，被删除的数据会被标记为无效 [11]。例如，在 Microsoft OneDrive 中，被删除的对象占已消耗存储容量的 26.5% [12]。（ii）一些存储系统采用异地更新以避免更新操作 [13], [14]。某些系统将更新后的数据写入新的存储空间，而不重写原数据，旧数据因此失效。随着无效数据增多，存储集群必须定期执行 GC，回收这些无效数据，以保证存储效率 [15]。

然而，在纠删码集群中实现高效垃圾回收颇具挑战。数据块在这类集群中按条带组织；为了保证同一条带中剩余有效数据块的冗余度，不能像多副本集群那样直接删除无效块。我们分析现有工作后，发现了一些尚未得到妥善解决的问题。

**网络流量大且流量负载不均衡。** 一种常见 GC 方法是收集各条带的有效数据块，并重新编码成新条带。例如，GOOD [13] 采用异地更新方法，重新编码无效块较多的条带中的有效数据块。然而，重新编码一个新条带需要读取 k 个有效数据块并生成 m 个校验块，使节点间网络流量放大 k + m 倍。此外，负责编码的节点还需要收集数据块并分发校验块，因此其流量负载重于其他数据节点和校验节点，进一步造成节点间流量负载不均。已有研究 BCStore [16] 旨在减少 GC 期间的磁盘 I/O 和网络流量。其核心思想是将有效数据块从无效块最多的条带迁移至无效块最少的条带，以使迁移的块数最少（例如，磁盘 I/O 最小）。但是，未经仔细规划的块迁移，以及无效块最少的条带所需的校验块更新，都可能在 GC 期间意外引入网络流量。此外，数据迁移会使多个条带中的无效数据被重写，这可以视为对无效数据的更新，因此 BCStore 必须同时处理多个条带的校验块更新。它没有显式设计多条带更新方法，而是随机调度传输路径，导致网络流量不均衡，进而增加 GC 时间。GC 期间较大的网络流量和不均衡的流量负载会延长 GC 时间，从而降低服务性能。

**数据读写性能低。** 现有工作着重降低 GC 期间的成本（如磁盘 I/O 和网络流量），却忽略了块布局对 GC 后数据读写性能的影响。就读取性能而言，属于同一条带的已迁移有效数据块可能集中在少数节点，导致并行文件访问时的读取性能下降。例如，BCStore 的随机数据迁移可能将同一条带剩余的有效数据块移到同一节点。因此，原条带中不同节点之间的并行读取会变成新条带内同一节点上的串行读取。就写入性能而言，回收部分条带会释放存储空间，可能形成不连续的空闲空间（称为碎片）。向这些不连续的空闲空间写入新数据时，频繁的磁盘寻道会使写入性能下降。遗憾的是，我们发现现有 GC 技术（如 GOOD 和 BCStore）均未考虑 GC 后的碎片问题，因此错失了在实际存储集群中提升写入性能的机会。随机块迁移和不连续的空闲空间都可能降低 GC 后的读写性能，对服务过程造成不可忽略的影响。

因此，如何同时实现快速垃圾回收，并在 GC 后保持快速存储服务，仍是尚未探索且并非轻而易举的问题。

不过，我们观察到，纠删码集群中存在有效数据块数量不同的条带。我们把有效数据块少于 k 个的条带称为非满条带，其他条带称为满条带。因此，我们的思路是选择两个非满条带，将它们合并成一个新的满条带。如果一个非满条带中的无效数据块布局与另一个非满条带中的有效数据块布局相同，就可以在本地生成新满条带，减少网络流量。这样既可以回收其中一个非满条带的存储空间，又能以条带为粒度迁移数据块，保证并行读取性能。接下来还有两个待解决的问题：如何找到能减少网络流量的合并方案，以及如何调度传输链路，使节点间的流量负载（如节点发送或接收的流量）均衡。

本文提出 FastGC，一种面向 RS 码的快速垃圾回收方法，旨在减少纠删码存储集群中的网络资源消耗，并维持系统性能。我们的贡献如下：

- 我们首次系统地研究纠删码集群中的垃圾回收问题，同时考虑 GC 期间的网络流量均衡和 GC 后的读写性能保持。我们利用条带合并来回收含有无效数据块的条带，并指出现有研究尚未解决的问题。（第 III 节）
- 我们提出 FastGC，以加速 RS 码的垃圾回收。FastGC 首先通过条带分组和位序列运算快速生成合并方案，高效减少网络流量。随后，它在合并过程中谨慎分配新条带的存储空间，消除影响写入性能的不连续碎片。最后，FastGC 贪心调度校验块更新的传输链路，以均衡节点间流量负载，并采用最大流算法充分利用带宽。（第 IV 节）
- 我们实现了 FastGC 原型，使用真实负载轨迹开展模拟和阿里云 ECS 实验，对其进行全面评估。评估结果表明，FastGC 可将网络流量减少 10.36%-81.22%，将 GC 时间减少 34.25%-72.36%。此外，我们还证明 FastGC 能有效均衡节点间网络流量，同时维持 GC 后的读写性能。（第 V、VI 节）

sections.title: II. BACKGROUND
sections.originalMarkdown: In this paper, we mainly focus on Reed-Solomon (RS) codes [4] that are popularly adopted in production clusters, including Ceph [17], HDFS [18], and QFS [19]. For simplicity, we use two parameters, k and m, to denote the RS codes (e.g., RS(k, m)). It collects k equal-size data blocks $\{d_1,\ldots,d_k\}$ from one or more file objects and encodes them into m equal-size parity blocks $\{p_1,\ldots,p_m\}$ by $p_j = \sum_{i=1}^{k}(x_{i,j} \cdot d_i)$, where $x_{i,j}$ $(1 \le i \le k)$ is the encoding coefficient used by $d_i$ to compute $p_j$. To ensure the node-level fault tolerance [8] and parallel file access [13], these k + m blocks collectively constitute a stripe and are distributed across k + m storage nodes. For example, Fig. 1 shows an erasure-coded cluster deployed with RS(k = 4, m = 2).
sections.translationMarkdown: 本文主要关注 Ceph [17]、HDFS [18] 和 QFS [19] 等生产集群广泛采用的 Reed-Solomon（RS）码 [4]。为简便起见，我们用 k 和 m 两个参数表示 RS 码（例如 RS(k, m)）。它从一个或多个文件对象中收集 k 个等大的数据块 $\{d_1,\ldots,d_k\}$，通过 $p_j = \sum_{i=1}^{k}(x_{i,j} \cdot d_i)$ 编码得到 m 个等大的校验块 $\{p_1,\ldots,p_m\}$，其中 $x_{i,j}$（$1 \le i \le k$）是用数据块 $d_i$ 计算 $p_j$ 时的编码系数。为保证节点级容错能力 [8] 和并行文件访问 [13]，这 k + m 个块共同组成一个条带，分布在 k + m 个存储节点上。例如，图 1 展示了采用 RS(k = 4, m = 2) 的纠删码集群。

sections.title: A. Erasure Coding in Clusters
sections.originalMarkdown:
In practice, repair and update are the two most common operations for erasure-coded clusters because of data failures and re-writing. As shown in Fig. 1, for repair, an RS(k, m) code needs to retrieve any k data or parity blocks from remaining blocks within a stripe to repair one failed block [8]. For update, if one or more data blocks are updated, one updated data or parity block collector collects the data delta (e.g., the difference between the new and old data) from updated data blocks and updates m parity blocks [9].

*Fig. 1. An example of erasure-coded clusters deployed with RS(k = 4, m = 2). Four data blocks are invalid in three stripes.*
sections.translationMarkdown:
在实践中，由于数据故障和重写，修复与更新是纠删码集群中最常见的两种操作。如图 1 所示，在修复时，RS(k, m) 码需要从同一条带剩余的块中读取任意 k 个数据块或校验块，以修复一个故障块 [8]。在更新时，如果一个或多个数据块被更新，某个已更新的数据块或校验块充当收集者，从已更新的数据块收集数据差量（即新旧数据之差），并更新 m 个校验块 [9]。

*图 1. 采用 RS(k = 4, m = 2) 的纠删码集群示例。三个条带中有四个数据块无效。*

sections.title: B. Garbage Collection in Clusters
sections.titleTranslation: B. 集群中的垃圾回收
sections.originalMarkdown:
When facing data deletion [12] or out-of-place update [14], the system will mark the old data block as invalid once the whole block is deleted or updated. Fig. 1 shows that four data blocks (marked in grey) are invalid for three stripes. For simplicity, we refer to the stripe with invalid blocks as a non-full stripe (e.g., S₁ and S₂) and vice versa as a full stripe (e.g. S₃). Therefore, the garbage collection mechanism recycles the non-full stripes to ensure storage efficiency. In the replication-based clusters, it only deletes all replica data for each invalid block to recycle storage space. However, since the data blocks are organized in stripes for erasure-coded clusters, the invalid block cannot be deleted directly. Otherwise, the stripe reliability will be degraded.

Several studies have been proposed to recycle invalid storage space. As shown in Fig. 2(a), GOOD [13] accordingly collects valid data blocks of the old non-full stripes and re-encodes them into new full stripes, then the old stripes can be released. It maintains the read parallelism of file access after GC, yet generating the new stripes will cause severe network traffic and prolong the GC process. GOOD also incurs unbalanced network traffic across nodes because of the congestion at nodes responsible for collecting and re-encoding. In Fig. 2(b), BCStore [16] migrates valid data blocks from stripes containing the most invalid blocks to those with the least. This migration can be considered an update of the invalid blocks. Consequently, all parity blocks of the stripes with the least invalid blocks also need to be updated. Although recycling the stripes with the most invalid blocks can minimize the number of moved blocks, BCStore does not carefully design the block migration and schedule the transmission routing for parity updates, which still introduces negligible and unbalanced network traffic. At the same time, the random migration of BCStore may concentrate these valid data blocks belonging to the same stripe or file on a few nodes, which decreases the read parallelism of file access after GC. In addition, another issue that needs to be addressed in existing studies is the write performance after GC. Recycling the non-full stripes will free the storage space and inadvertently result in discontinuous free spaces (called fragments). When writing new data to the fragments, it needs frequent disk seeks and further decreases the write performance. Reducing network traffic and GC time caused by garbage collection is critical but cannot come at the expense of the problems above.

We summarize existing garbage collection studies in Table I. Overall, existing methods either incur high and unbalanced network traffic during GC or neglect the read and write performance after GC. It motivates us to propose a systematical FastGC method to solve these issues in this paper.

*Fig. 2. Existing garbage collection methods.*

*Table I. Summary of existing garbage collection methods.*

| Methods | Network traffic (During GC) | Load rate (During GC) | GC latency (During GC) | Read perf. (After GC) | Write perf. (After GC) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GOOD [13] | high | high | high | medium | high |
| BCStore [16] | medium | high | medium | low | low |
| FastGC (Our) | low | low | low | high | high |

遇到数据删除 [12] 或异地更新 [14] 时，一旦整个旧数据块被删除或更新，系统就会将其标记为无效。图 1 展示了三个条带中的四个无效数据块（以灰色标记）。为简便起见，我们将包含无效块的条带称为非满条带（如 S₁、S₂），将不含无效块的条带称为满条带（如 S₃）。因此，垃圾回收机制通过回收非满条带来保证存储效率。在多副本集群中，只需删除每个无效块的所有副本数据即可回收存储空间。然而，在纠删码集群中，数据块按条带组织，不能直接删除无效块，否则会降低条带的可靠性。

已有多项研究提出了回收无效存储空间的方法。如图 2(a) 所示，GOOD [13] 收集旧非满条带中的有效数据块，将其重新编码为新满条带，随后释放旧条带。它保持了 GC 后文件访问的读取并行度，但生成新条带会产生大量网络流量，延长 GC 过程。由于负责收集和重新编码的节点发生拥塞，GOOD 还造成节点间网络流量不均衡。在图 2(b) 中，BCStore [16] 将有效数据块从无效块最多的条带迁移至无效块最少的条带。这一迁移可以视为对无效块的更新，因此无效块最少的条带中的所有校验块也必须更新。虽然回收无效块最多的条带可以最大限度减少迁移块数，但 BCStore 没有仔细设计块迁移和校验块更新的传输路径调度，仍会引入少量且不均衡的网络流量。同时，BCStore 的随机迁移可能使同一条带或文件的有效数据块集中到少数节点，降低 GC 后文件访问的读取并行度。此外，现有研究尚需解决的另一个问题是 GC 后的写入性能。回收非满条带会释放存储空间，并无意间形成不连续的空闲空间（称为碎片）。向碎片写入新数据时，需要频繁磁盘寻道，进一步降低写入性能。减少垃圾回收造成的网络流量和 GC 时间至关重要，但不能以加剧上述问题为代价。

我们在表 I 中总结了现有垃圾回收研究。总体而言，现有方法要么在 GC 期间产生大量且不均衡的网络流量，要么忽略 GC 后的读写性能。这促使我们提出系统化的 FastGC 方法来解决这些问题。

*图 2. 现有垃圾回收方法。*

*表 I. 现有垃圾回收方法总结。*

sections.title: III. OBSERVATIONS AND FORMULATION
sections.originalMarkdown:
When garbage collection is triggered, we observe that the erasure-coded cluster has non-full stripes with different numbers of valid data blocks. Therefore, the main idea is to select two non-full stripes from the currently all non-full stripes, such that the two stripes can be merged into a new full stripe. To clarify, we use the block placement of S₁ and S₂ in Fig. 1 as an example. As shown in Fig. 3, the merging process comprises the following three steps:

- Step 1: Migrating valid data blocks in one non-full stripe (called recycled stripe) to the node where the invalid data blocks are located in another non-full stripe (called updated stripe).
- Step 2: Substituting the invalid data blocks in the updated stripe with the migrated data blocks such that it can construct a new full stripe for the updated stripe.
- Step 3: Updating all parity blocks in the updated stripe via applying RackCU [9]. It selects the sole collector block from updated data or parity blocks, collects data deltas, and updates the parity blocks.

*Fig. 3. Merging of stripes S₁ and S₂.*

触发垃圾回收时，我们观察到纠删码集群中存在有效数据块数量不同的非满条带。因此，核心思路是从现有全部非满条带中选择两个，使其能够合并成一个新的满条带。为说明这一点，我们以图 1 中 S₁ 和 S₂ 的块放置位置为例。如图 3 所示，合并过程包括以下三个步骤：

- 步骤 1：将一个非满条带（称为被回收条带）中的有效数据块迁移到另一个非满条带（称为被更新条带）中无效数据块所在的节点。
- 步骤 2：用迁移来的数据块替换被更新条带中的无效数据块，从而为该条带构造新的满条带。
- 步骤 3：使用 RackCU [9] 更新被更新条带中的全部校验块。它从已更新的数据块或校验块中选择唯一一个块作为收集者，收集数据差量并更新校验块。

sections.title: A. Motivation and Observation
sections.originalMarkdown:
The merging idea can maintain the original distributions of valid data blocks for two merged stripes, which has no impact on the original read performance. Motivated by the above example, we argue that the merging idea still manufactures new problems and has the following observations.

**Observation#1: Reasonable selection of merged stripes can reduce network traffic.** We first notice that there exist network traffic during migrating (Step 1), and the selected two stripes directly determine the migration network traffic. Based on the data layout in Fig. 1, suppose the valid block of S₂ is located in N₄. When the valid data blocks in the recycled stripe are at the node where the invalid data blocks are located in the updated stripe, we can optimally merge these two non-full stripes into a new full stripe with less migration network traffic. Hence, as shown in Fig. 4, we can directly substitute the invalid data block b₁,₄ in S₁ with the valid data block b₂,₄ in S₂, which has no migration network traffic in Step 1.

While optimal merging can reduce the network traffic, how to quickly and effectively select two stripes to merge from a larger number of non-full stripes remains non-trivial. Specifically, suppose the cluster deployed RS(k, m) has s non-full stripes. The complexity of computing migration cost for two non-full stripes is O(k) (e.g., check the layout of valid data blocks in recycled stripe). If we naively traverse all s non-full stripes to obtain the merged pair, the total time complexity is O(s² · k), which is time-consuming for larger s and k.

**Observation#2: Recycling of stripes introduces storage fragments, which decreases the write performance.** Second, the storage space of recycled stripes will be released after GC, which causes discontinuous storage fragments in disks. For example, in Fig. 5, releasing the storage space of S₂ will generate a free fragment space between S₁ and S₃. If more recycled stripes are released, these fragment spaces will become dispersed. These fragment spaces may affect the writing performance when writing new data because the disk needs to move the mechanic disk head to each free space. Although we can move the remaining stripes to fill the fragment spaces after GC, it will inevitably incur significant disk I/Os. Therefore, we also need to consider the blocks storage allocation in updated stripes to eliminate the fragments.

**Observation#3: The unbalanced network traffic across nodes prolongs the GC procedure.** After migrating, the parity blocks in updated stripes must also be updated (Step 3). Some update-efficient schemes [9], [20], [21] are proposed to reduce the network traffic for single-stripe updates. For example, the latest study, RackCU [9], designs an optimal update mechanism to minimize the network traffic. It selects the sole collector from all updated data and parity blocks to collect the data delta from updated data blocks. The collector computes the parity deltas and updates the parity blocks. However, merging in multiple stripes will incur multi-stripe updates during GC, and the random collector selection for multiple stripes may cause unbalanced upload and download network traffic across nodes, which easily prolongs the GC procedure and has yet to be considered by existing studies.

Fig. 6 presents an example that illustrates the inter-node upload and download traffic of two updated stripes during GC, and we only display the updated data and parity blocks in updated stripes. For example, the updated blocks of the first updated stripe in Fig. 6 are based on the new stripe S₁ in Fig. 5. As shown in Fig. 6(a), if we select two blocks in N₄ as collectors for two updated stripes, N₄ is the most traffic load node and needs to upload four blocks to other nodes. As a comparison, in Fig. 6(b), if we select blocks from different nodes as collectors (e.g., N₃ and N₅), the highest traffic load is two, and the inter-node traffic distribution is more balanced. Since existing clusters extensively support full-duplex parallel technology [8], [22], most upload and download traffic may become the performance bottleneck during GC. Achieving more balanced traffic across nodes can reduce the GC time.

*Fig. 4. Optimal stripe merging.*

*Fig. 5. Discontinuous storage fragments.*

*Fig. 6. Two different network traffic distributions.*

合并思路可以保持两个被合并条带中有效数据块原有的分布，因此不会影响原有的读取性能。受到上述例子的启发，我们认为合并思路仍会产生新问题，并有以下观察。

**观察 1：合理选择待合并条带可以减少网络流量。** 首先，我们注意到迁移（步骤 1）期间会产生网络流量，而选取的两个条带直接决定迁移流量。基于图 1 的数据布局，假设 S₂ 的有效块位于 N₄。当被回收条带的有效数据块恰好位于被更新条带的无效数据块所在节点时，就可以以较少的迁移流量，将两个非满条带最优合并为一个新满条带。因此，如图 4 所示，可以直接用 S₂ 中的有效数据块 b₂,₄ 替换 S₁ 中的无效数据块 b₁,₄，步骤 1 不产生迁移网络流量。

虽然最优合并可以减少网络流量，但从大量非满条带中快速、有效地选择两个待合并条带并不简单。具体而言，假设采用 RS(k, m) 的集群中有 s 个非满条带。计算两个非满条带之间迁移成本的复杂度是 O(k)（例如，需要检查被回收条带中有效数据块的布局）。如果朴素地遍历所有 s 个非满条带来寻找合并配对，总时间复杂度为 O(s² · k)，当 s 和 k 较大时非常耗时。

**观察 2：回收条带会产生存储碎片，降低写入性能。** 其次，GC 后，被回收条带的存储空间会释放，在磁盘上形成不连续的存储碎片。例如，图 5 中释放 S₂ 的存储空间后，会在 S₁ 和 S₃ 之间产生一块空闲碎片空间。如果释放更多被回收条带，这些碎片空间将更加分散。写入新数据时，磁盘需要将机械磁头移到每个空闲空间，因此碎片可能影响写入性能。虽然可以在 GC 后移动其余条带以填补碎片空间，但这不可避免地造成大量磁盘 I/O。因此，还需考虑被更新条带的块存储分配，以消除碎片。

**观察 3：节点间网络流量不均衡会延长 GC 过程。** 迁移后，被更新条带中的校验块也必须更新（步骤 3）。已有一些更新效率较高的方案 [9], [20], [21] 用于减少单条带更新的网络流量。例如，最近的研究 RackCU [9] 设计了一种最优更新机制，以最大限度减少网络流量。它从所有已更新的数据块和校验块中选择唯一的收集者，收集已更新数据块的数据差量。收集者计算校验差量并更新校验块。然而，合并多个条带会在 GC 期间引发多条带更新；若随机选择多个条带的收集者，可能造成节点间上传和下载流量不均，容易延长 GC 过程。现有研究尚未考虑这一问题。

图 6 给出了 GC 期间两个被更新条带的节点间上传与下载流量示例，其中仅展示条带中已更新的数据块和校验块。例如，图 6 中第一个被更新条带的已更新块取自图 5 中的新条带 S₁。如图 6(a) 所示，如果选择 N₄ 中的两个块分别作为两个被更新条带的收集者，N₄ 将成为流量负载最高的节点，需要向其他节点上传四个块。相比之下，在图 6(b) 中，如果从不同节点（如 N₃、N₅）选择收集者，最大流量负载为两个块，节点间的流量分布更加均衡。由于现有集群广泛支持全双工并行技术 [8], [22]，上传或下载流量的峰值可能成为 GC 期间的性能瓶颈。让节点间流量更加均衡可以缩短 GC 时间。

*图 4. 最优条带合并。*

sections.title: B. Model Formulation
sections.originalMarkdown:
We next formalize the GC problem and establish the optimization models. Suppose that s stripes {Sᵢ | 1 ≤ i ≤ s} to be recycled are distributed among n storage nodes {Nᵢ | 1 ≤ i ≤ n}, and each stripe is encoded by RS(k, m). Let bᵢ,ⱼ indicate that a block of stripe Sᵢ is located in node Nⱼ. Let MT and UT be the migrating and updating network traffic when recycling s stripes. Thus, the total network traffic GT during GC is

$$GT = MT + UT \tag{1}$$

Let Tuᵢ and Tdᵢ be the upload and download traffic for node Nᵢ, respectively. Then, the maximum traffic load on Nᵢ can be denoted by Tᵢ, where Tᵢ = max(Tuᵢ, Tdᵢ). We define the load rate of cluster LR as the ratio of the maximum load of network traffic across each node to the average load of network traffic over the n nodes.

$$LR = \frac{\max\{T_i \mid 1 \le i \le n\}}{\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} T_i}{n}} \tag{2}$$

Based on the above Observation 2, recycling of stripes introduces storage fragments, and each free fragment space requires one disk seek when writing new data. Therefore, reducing the number of discontinuous spaces can improve the write performance after GC.

To achieve the minimum GC time and keep service performance, we want to achieve two objectives as follows.

- Objective 1: Minimize the network traffic GT and balance the inter-node upload and download traffic by minimizing LR.
- Objective 2: Maintain the valid data block distributions within a stripe and reduce the number of fragment spaces to keep the read/write performance.

接下来，我们将 GC 问题形式化，并建立优化模型。假设待回收的 s 个条带 {Sᵢ | 1 ≤ i ≤ s} 分布在 n 个存储节点 {Nᵢ | 1 ≤ i ≤ n} 上，且每个条带都采用 RS(k, m) 编码。用 bᵢ,ⱼ 表示条带 Sᵢ 的一个块位于节点 Nⱼ。用 MT 和 UT 分别表示回收 s 个条带时的迁移与更新网络流量。那么，GC 期间的总网络流量 GT 为

$$GT = MT + UT \\tag{1}$$

设 Tuᵢ 和 Tdᵢ 分别为节点 Nᵢ 的上传和下载流量。节点 Nᵢ 的最大流量负载记为 Tᵢ，其中 Tᵢ = max(Tuᵢ, Tdᵢ)。我们将集群负载率 LR 定义为所有节点中的最大网络流量负载与 n 个节点平均网络流量负载之比。

$$LR = \frac{\max\{T_i \mid 1 \le i \le n\}}{\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} T_i}{n}} \tag{2}$$

根据上述观察 2，回收条带会产生存储碎片，而向新数据写入每个空闲碎片空间时都需要一次磁盘寻道。因此，减少不连续空间的数量能够改善 GC 后的写入性能。

为了最小化 GC 时间，同时保持服务性能，我们希望实现以下两个目标：

- 目标 1：最小化网络流量 GT，并通过最小化 LR 使节点间上传和下载流量均衡。
- 目标 2：维持同一条带内有效数据块的分布，并减少碎片空间数量，以保持读写性能。

sections.originalMarkdown: We now present the design of FastGC, a fast garbage collection method that aims to achieve the two objectives in Sec. III-B. It builds on three design components: generating merge solution (Sec. IV-A), eliminating fragment spaces (Sec. IV-B), and balancing traffic load (Sec. IV-C).

sections.title: A. Generating Merge Solution
sections.titleTranslation: A. 生成条带合并方案
sections.originalMarkdown:
As stated in Observation 1, traversing all s stripes to find the merge solution has a prohibitive computation complexity (e.g., O($s^2\cdot k$)), and the complexity comes from the traversal of stripes O($s^2$) and the computation of merge costs O($k$). Therefore, we classify the stripes into different sets based on the number of valid data blocks and traverse fewer stripes to find the optimal merge solution. In addition, we adopt the bit sequences operations instead of the logical traversal operations to compute the merge cost for two stripes to be merged. 

Algorithm Details: Algorithm 1 shows the pseudo-code and returns the merge solution Solu. Before the Alg. 1 is called, we pre-process these non-full stripes and construct the set Vi(1 ≤ i ≤ k − 1), indicating that each stripe in Vi has i valid data blocks. First, Alg. 1 initializes the set Solu as NULL (Line 1) to record the merged stripe pairs. For an unmerged non-full stripe Sx in Vi (e.g., has i valid data blocks), it then tries each unmerged non-full stripe Sy in Vk−i (e.g., has k − i valid data blocks) to merge (Lines 2-7). Specifically, if Sx and Sy can be optimally merged (e.g., without migration network traffic), it sets y* as y and jumps out of the for-loop in Line 5 (Lines 9-11); otherwise, if Sy brings merge cost saving over the minimum merge cost c* currently found (Line 12), then it records currently Sy and updates the current minimal cost c* (Line 13). After traversing all stripes in Vk−i, Alg. 1 determines the recycled and updated stripe from Sx and Sy* (Lines 14-18). If Sx is the recycled stripe and Sy* is the updated stripe (Sx → Sy* ), we need to migrate i valid data blocks in Sx to the node where the invalid data blocks are located in Sy* and update m parity blocks in Sy* and vice versa. Finally, Alg. 1 appends Sx and Sy* to Solu and starts the next for-loop in Line 3. We also indicate that there are unmerged stripes in set Vi or Vk−i after traversing all stripes in Vi, because the number of stripes in Vi and Vk−i may be not equal. Hence, we apply BCStore [16] to recycle the remaining unmerged stripes in Vi or Vk−i (Line 19). 

**Algorithm 1: Generating Merge Solution.**

Input: RS$(k,m)$, a set of stripe $\{S_i\mid 1\le i\le s\}$, sets $\{V_i\mid 1\le i\le k-1\}$  
Output: a merge solution $Solu$

```text
1  Solu = ∅
2  for i = 1 to k/2 do
3      for each stripe S_x in V_i do
4          c* = Max_value, y* = -1
5          for each stripe S_y in V_{k-i} do
6              if S_x or S_y has been merged || x == y then
7                  continue
8              c = compute merge cost of S_x and S_y via bit sequences
9              if S_x and S_y are optimal merging then
10                 y* = y
11                 break
12             else if c < c* then
13                 y* = y, c* = c
14         if y* != -1 then
15             if merge cost of S_x → S_{y*} is less than S_{y*} → S_x then
16                 Solu += (S_x, S_{y*})
17             else
18                 Solu += (S_{y*}, S_x)
19 return Solu
```

To further reduce the time complexity, we exploit the bit sequence to quickly compute the merge cost (including migration and update cost) in Line 8. We need to check the layout of all valid data blocks in the recycled stripe to compute the migration cost, which takes O($k$) time. We can compute the update cost by the number of invalid data blocks in the updated stripe, which takes O(1) time (e.g., the minimum update cost for r updated data blocks is r + m − 1 blocks via RackCU [9]). Hence, we next reduce the time complexity of migration cost computation. We construct two bit sequences, Rbi and Ubi, for each stripe Si, and each bit sequence (w1,w2,…,wn) specifies the blocks layout. If Si is a recycled stripe and block bi,j is the valid data block, we set wj = 1 for sequence Rbi, and the rest bits is 0. If Si is an updated stripe and block bi,j is the invalid data block, we set wj = 0 for sequence Ubi, and the rest bits is 1. Then, we perform AND operations on the bit sequences corresponding to the recycled and updated stripe and use the built-in functions __builtin_popcount() [23] in C++ to compute the number of 1-bits in the result, which is the migration cost. For example, in Fig. 8(a) (e.g., n = 6 storage nodes), the bit sequences for stripe S1 and S3 are $$Rb_1=(001100)\quad\text{and}\quad Ub_1=(111100)$$

$$Rb_3=(110000)\quad\text{and}\quad Ub_3=(110011)$$ 

If we merge the S1 to S3 (S1 → S3), the corresponding AND operation is $$Rb_1 \& Ub_3=(001100) \& (110011)=(000000)$$ 

The result has zero 1-bits, and the migration cost is zero. In Fig. 8(a), two valid data blocks in S1 (e.g., b1,3 and b1,4) are located at the node (e.g., N3 and N4) where the invalid data block (e.g., b3,3 and b3,4) is located in S3, and we can migrate them locally. 

However, if we merge the S3 to S1 (S3 → S1), the corresponding AND operation is $$Rb_3 \& Ub_1=(110000) \& (111100)=(110000)$$ 

The result has two 1-bits, and the migration cost is two. In Fig. 8(a), we need to migrate two valid data blocks in S3 (e.g., b3,1 and b3,2) to the node (e.g., N5 and N6) where the invalid data block (e.g., b1,5 and b1,6) is located in S1. 

Compared to logical traversal operations within milliseconds, the AND operations and built-in functions can be completed within nanoseconds, and the time complexity is approximately O(1). In addition, the bit sequences operations significantly reduce the time complexity of merge solution generation and only consume a small amount of storage overhead (for s = 1000, n = 15, the metadata consumes about n · s · 2 = 1.83KB). 

Multi-stripe merging: After Alg. 1, some stripes cannot be merged in pairs. In order to recycle these stripes, we migrate the valid data blocks in one stripe to the positions of the invalid blocks in multiple stripes. BCStore [16] migrates valid data blocks from stripes containing the most invalid blocks to those with the least. However, this approach may not effectively reduce the network traffic during the recycling process. As shown in Fig. 7(a), S3 has the most invalid blocks. Therefore, BCStore migrates the valid blocks in S3 to S1 and S2. The network traffic is 6. However, in Fig. 7(a), merging S1 with S2 and S3 result in less network traffic. To this end, we propose Algorithm 2 to effectively recycle the remaining stripes. 

**Algorithm 2: Merging for Multiple Stripes.**

Input: RS$(k,m)$, a set of stripes that have not merged by Alg. 1, the maximum number of stripes $w$  
Output: a merge solution $Solu$

```text
1  Solu = ∅
2  for i = 3 to w do
3      S = find i unmerged stripes that meet the merging condition
4      c* = Max_value, x* = -1
5      for each stripe S_x in S do
6          S′ = S - S_x
7          c = compute merge cost of S_x → S′ via bit sequences
8          if c < c* then
9              x* = x, c* = c
10     S′ = S - S_{x*}
11     Solu += (S_{x*}, S′)
12 return Solu
```

Fig. 7. Multi-stripe merging for BCStore and FastGC.

Fig. 8. Example of generating merge solution for six non-full stripes.

Alg. 2 uses a parameter w to control the number of stripes merged in a single operation. Since Alg. 1 adopts the method of merging two stripes, Alg. 2 successively selects 3, 4,… , w stripes to complete the merging (Line 2). It first finds i unmerged stripes that meet the following merging condition and record them by S (Line 3). Suppose that the number of valid data blocks for all i stripes is nv1,…, nvi. Thus, the merging condition is k = (k − nv1) + … + (k − nvi). The merging condition ensures that recycling one stripe Sx can provide nvx valid data blocks to fill the i − 1 stripes. Next, Alg. 2 tries each stripe Sx as the recycled stripe in S, computes the merge cost via bit sequences, and generates the merge solution with minimum merge cost (Lines 4-12). Note that the bit sequence operation in the multi-stripe merging still uses the AND operation. For example, in Fig. 7(a), if we merge the S3 with S1 and S2, the corresponding AND operation is $$Rb_3 \& Ub_1 \& Ub_2=(001100) \& (111100) \& (001100)=(001100)$$ 

An Example: We elaborate on Alg. 1 via an example. As shown in Fig. 8(a), the cluster deployed with RS(k = 4,m = 2) has n = 6 storage nodes and s = 6 non-full stripes. Before the Alg. 1 is called, we construct the set Vi(1 ≤ i ≤ 3) and binary bit values for each stripe. The Fig. 8(b) shows the computation procedure. When i = 1 and Sx = S4, we traverse all stripes in Vk−i = V3 and find that the merged pair (S4,S5) has the minimum merge cost. Thus, we append it to Solu. Then, we traverse the remaining stripes and search the merge pair in the same way. 

Time Complexity: We next analyse the time complexity of Alg. 1 and 2. For the first foor-loop in Alg. 1, we only traverse half of the sets (O($k/2$)) because the algorithm traverses Vk−i while traversing Vi. If each set has the same number of non-full stripes, the number of stripes in each Vi is s=k. Thus, the time complexity of the second and third for-loop (Lines 3 and 5) are O($s/k\cdot s/k$) = O($s^2/k^2$). Computing the merge cost takes O(1) time in Line 8. Since each stripe in Vi or Vk−i has the same valid blocks, it only takes O(1) time in Line 19. The overall time complexity of Alg. 1 is O($k/2\cdot s^2/k^2\cdot 1$) = O($s^2/k$). For Alg. 2, finding unmerged stripes that meet the merging condition needs O($((s/k)^w)$) time, and the time complexity of Lines 4-11 is O(w). Therefore, the overall time complexity of Alg. 2 is O($w\cdot((s/k)^w+w)$) ≈ O($w\cdot(s/k)^w$).

如观察 1 所述，遍历全部 $s$ 个条带来寻找合并方案会产生难以承受的计算复杂度（例如 $O(s^2\cdot k)$）。其中，遍历条带的复杂度为 $O(s^2)$，计算合并代价的复杂度为 $O(k)$。因此，我们按照有效数据块的数量将条带分到不同集合，只遍历较少的条带来寻找最优合并方案。此外，我们使用位序列操作来计算两个条带的合并代价，而非逐项进行逻辑遍历。

**算法细节：**算法 1 给出伪代码并返回合并方案 $Solu$。调用算法 1 之前，我们预处理这些未满条带并构造集合 $V_i(1\le i\le k-1)$，其中每个条带都包含 $i$ 个有效数据块。首先，算法 1 将 $Solu$ 初始化为空（第 1 行），用来记录合并条带对。对于 $V_i$ 中尚未合并的条带 $S_x$（例如含有 $i$ 个有效数据块），它依次尝试与 $V_{k-i}$ 中每个尚未合并的条带 $S_y$（例如含有 $k-i$ 个有效数据块）合并（第 2–7 行）。具体来说，如果 $S_x$ 和 $S_y$ 能够最优合并（例如不产生迁移网络流量），则把 $y^*$ 设为 $y$ 并跳出第 5 行的循环（第 9–11 行）；否则，如果 $S_y$ 比目前找到的最小合并代价 $c^*$ 更节省代价（第 12 行），则记录当前的 $S_y$，并更新最小代价 $c^*$（第 13 行）。遍历 $V_{k-i}$ 中全部条带后，算法 1 在 $S_x$ 和 $S_{y^*}$ 之间确定回收条带与更新条带（第 14–18 行）。如果 $S_x$ 是回收条带，$S_{y^*}$ 是更新条带（$S_x\rightarrow S_{y^*}$），就需要将 $S_x$ 中的 $i$ 个有效数据块迁移到 $S_{y^*}$ 中无效数据块所在的节点，并更新 $S_{y^*}$ 的 $m$ 个校验块；反向合并同理。最后，算法 1 将 $S_x$ 和 $S_{y^*}$ 加入 $Solu$，并开始第 3 行的下一轮循环。我们还指出，遍历完 $V_i$ 中的全部条带后，由于 $V_i$ 与 $V_{k-i}$ 的条带数可能不相等，任一集合中都可能留下未合并的条带。因此，我们使用 BCStore [16] 回收 $V_i$ 或 $V_{k-i}$ 中剩余的未合并条带（第 19 行）。

**算法 1：生成合并方案。**

输入：RS$(k,m)$、条带集合 $\{S_i\mid 1\le i\le s\}$、集合 $\{V_i\mid 1\le i\le k-1\}$  
输出：合并方案 $Solu$

```text
1  Solu = ∅
2  对 i = 1 到 k/2 执行
3      对 V_i 中每个条带 S_x 执行
4          c* = Max_value, y* = -1
5          对 V_{k-i} 中每个条带 S_y 执行
6              若 S_x 或 S_y 已合并，或 x == y，则
7                  继续
8              通过位序列计算 S_x 与 S_y 的合并代价 c
9              若 S_x 与 S_y 可最优合并，则
10                 y* = y
11                 跳出循环
12             否则，若 c < c*，则
13                 y* = y, c* = c
14         若 y* != -1，则
15             若 S_x → S_{y*} 的合并代价小于 S_{y*} → S_x，则
16                 Solu += (S_x, S_{y*})
17             否则
18                 Solu += (S_{y*}, S_x)
19 返回 Solu
```

为了进一步降低时间复杂度，我们使用位序列快速计算第 8 行的合并代价（包括迁移与更新代价）。计算迁移代价需要检查回收条带中全部有效数据块的布局，耗时 $O(k)$。更新代价可以通过更新条带中的无效数据块数量计算，耗时 $O(1)$（例如，通过 RackCU [9] 更新 $r$ 个数据块的最小更新代价为 $r+m-1$ 个块）。因此，我们接下来降低迁移代价的计算复杂度。我们为每个条带 $S_i$ 构造两个位序列 $Rb_i$ 和 $Ub_i$，每个位序列 $(w_1,w_2,\ldots,w_n)$ 表示块布局。如果 $S_i$ 是回收条带，且块 $b_{i,j}$ 是有效数据块，则将 $Rb_i$ 中的 $w_j$ 设为 1，其余位设为 0。如果 $S_i$ 是更新条带，且块 $b_{i,j}$ 是无效数据块，则将 $Ub_i$ 中的 $w_j$ 设为 0，其余位设为 1。随后，对回收条带与更新条带对应的位序列执行 AND 操作，再使用 C++ 内置函数 `__builtin_popcount()` [23] 计算结果中 1 的个数，即迁移代价。例如，在图 8(a) 中（有 $n=6$ 个存储节点），条带 $S_1$ 和 $S_3$ 的位序列为：
$$Rb_1=(001100)\quad\text{and}\quad Ub_1=(111100)$$

$$Rb_3=(110000)\quad\text{and}\quad Ub_3=(110011)$$

如果将 $S_1$ 合并到 $S_3$（$S_1\rightarrow S_3$），对应的 AND 操作为：
$$Rb_1\ \&\ Ub_3=(001100)\ \&\ (110011)=(000000)$$

结果中没有 1，因此迁移代价为零。在图 8(a) 中，$S_1$ 的两个有效数据块（例如 $b_{1,3}$ 和 $b_{1,4}$）位于 $S_3$ 中无效数据块（例如 $b_{3,3}$ 和 $b_{3,4}$）所在节点（例如 $N_3$ 和 $N_4$），因此可以在节点内迁移。

但是，如果将 $S_3$ 合并到 $S_1$（$S_3\rightarrow S_1$），对应的 AND 操作为：
$$Rb_3\ \&\ Ub_1=(110000)\ \&\ (111100)=(110000)$$

结果有两个 1，因此迁移代价为 2。在图 8(a) 中，需要将 $S_3$ 的两个有效数据块（例如 $b_{3,1}$ 和 $b_{3,2}$）迁移到 $S_1$ 中无效数据块（例如 $b_{1,5}$ 和 $b_{1,6}$）所在的节点（例如 $N_5$ 和 $N_6$）。

相比以毫秒计的逻辑遍历操作，AND 操作和内置函数可以在纳秒级完成，其时间复杂度近似为 $O(1)$。此外，位序列操作显著降低了生成合并方案的时间复杂度，且仅占用少量存储空间（当 $s=1000,n=15$ 时，元数据约占 $n\cdot s\cdot 2=1.83\mathrm{KB}$）。

**多条带合并：**算法 1 执行后，部分条带仍无法两两合并。为了回收这些条带，我们将一个条带中的有效数据块迁移到多个条带的无效块位置。BCStore [16] 将无效块最多的条带中的有效块迁移到无效块最少的条带。但是，这种方式不一定能有效降低回收过程中的网络流量。如图 7(a) 所示，$S_3$ 的无效块最多，因此 BCStore 将 $S_3$ 中的有效块迁移到 $S_1$ 和 $S_2$，网络流量为 6。然而，在图 7(a) 中，将 $S_1$ 与 $S_2$、$S_3$ 合并产生的网络流量更少。为此，我们提出算法 2，以有效回收剩余条带。

**算法 2：多条带合并。**

输入：RS$(k,m)$、未被算法 1 合并的条带集合、最大条带数 $w$  
输出：合并方案 $Solu$

```text
1  Solu = ∅
2  对 i = 3 到 w 执行
3      S = 查找满足合并条件的 i 个未合并条带
4      c* = Max_value, x* = -1
5      对 S 中每个条带 S_x 执行
6          S′ = S - S_x
7          通过位序列计算 S_x → S′ 的合并代价 c
8          若 c < c*，则
9              x* = x, c* = c
10     S′ = S - S_{x*}
11     Solu += (S_{x*}, S′)
12 返回 Solu
```

图 7. BCStore 与 FastGC 的多条带合并。

图 8. 六个未满条带的合并方案生成示例。

算法 2 使用参数 $w$ 控制一次操作中合并的条带数。由于算法 1 采用两个条带合并的方法，算法 2 依次选择 3、4、……、$w$ 个条带完成合并（第 2 行）。它首先找出满足下述合并条件的 $i$ 个未合并条带，并将其记为 $S$（第 3 行）。设这 $i$ 个条带的有效数据块数量分别为 $nv_1,\ldots,nv_i$。合并条件为 $k=(k-nv_1)+\cdots+(k-nv_i)$。该条件保证回收一个条带 $S_x$ 提供的 $nv_x$ 个有效数据块能够填充另外 $i-1$ 个条带。接下来，算法 2 依次尝试将 $S$ 中每个条带 $S_x$ 作为回收条带，通过位序列计算合并代价，生成代价最小的合并方案（第 4–12 行）。注意，多条带合并中的位序列操作仍然使用 AND。例如，在图 7(a) 中，若将 $S_3$ 与 $S_1$、$S_2$ 合并，对应的 AND 操作为：
$$Rb_3\ \&\ Ub_1\ \&\ Ub_2=(001100)\ \&\ (111100)\ \&\ (001100)=(001100)$$

**示例：**我们通过一个示例说明算法 1。如图 8(a) 所示，采用 RS$(k=4,m=2)$ 的集群有 $n=6$ 个存储节点和 $s=6$ 个未满条带。调用算法 1 前，我们构造集合 $V_i(1\le i\le 3)$ 以及每个条带的二进制位值。图 8(b) 给出了计算过程。当 $i=1$ 且 $S_x=S_4$ 时，我们遍历 $V_{k-i}=V_3$ 中所有条带，发现合并条带对 $(S_4,S_5)$ 的合并代价最小，于是将其加入 $Solu$。然后以相同方式遍历剩余条带并寻找合并条带对。

**时间复杂度：**下面分析算法 1 和 2 的时间复杂度。算法 1 的第一层 for 循环只遍历一半集合（$O(k/2)$），因为遍历 $V_i$ 时算法也会遍历 $V_{k-i}$。如果每个集合的未满条带数量相同，则每个 $V_i$ 中有 $s/k$ 个条带。因此，第二、三层 for 循环（第 3、5 行）的复杂度为 $O((s/k)\cdot(s/k))=O(s^2/k^2)$。第 8 行计算合并代价耗时 $O(1)$。由于 $V_i$ 或 $V_{k-i}$ 中各条带的有效块数相同，第 19 行也只耗时 $O(1)$。因此，算法 1 的总体时间复杂度为 $O((k/2)\cdot(s^2/k^2)\cdot1)=O(s^2/k)$。对于算法 2，寻找满足合并条件的未合并条带耗时 $O((s/k)^w)$，第 4–11 行的时间复杂度为 $O(w)$。因此，算法 2 的总体时间复杂度为 $O(w\cdot((s/k)^w+w))\approx O(w\cdot(s/k)^w)$。

sections.title: B. Eliminating Fragment Spaces
sections.originalMarkdown:
As stated in Observation 2, the released spaces are scattered in the disk, which incurs additional disk seeks when writing new data. For example, in Fig. 9(a), it causes 3 fragments for the merge solution of Fig. 8(b) after merging. A naive way is to move all blocks of S5 to fill the free spaces of S1 to eliminate the fragments, but it still introduces an additional 12 disk I/Os (e.g., read and write six blocks). When handling a tremendous number of stripes, this way will consume the bus bandwidth resources, thereby disturbing the foreground jobs. Alternatively, we designed Algorithm 3, whose main idea is to carefully migrate the blocks to the predetermined continuous storage space during merging; in other words, we should avoid introducing new fragment when merging stripes. 

**Algorithm 3: Eliminating Fragment Spaces.**

Input: a merge solution $Solu$

```text
1  for each node N_i do
2      predetermined storage location Loc for N_i
3      for each (S_x, S_y) in Solu do
4          if b_{x,i} is valid data, b_{y,i}(∈ Loc) is invalid data then
5              migrate b_{x,i} to b_{y,i}
6          if b_{x,i}(∈ Loc) is invalid data, b_{y,i}(∉ Loc) is valid data then
7              migrate b_{y,i} to b_{x,i}
8      for each (S_x, S_y) in Solu do
9          if b_{x,i}(∉ Loc) is valid data, b_{y,i}(∉ Loc) is invalid data then
10             obtain the free storage space floc from Loc
11             migrate b_{x,i} to b_{y,floc}
12         if b_{y,i}(∉ Loc) is valid data or parity then
13             obtain the free storage space floc from Loc
14             migrate b_{y,i} to b_{y,floc}
```

Fig. 9. Example of eliminating fragments for the merge solution of Fig. 8(b).

Algorithm Details: Alg. 3 needs a predetermined continuous storage location Loc for each node Ni, which includes the length len and start address sa. Let nv be the number of valid data blocks for s stripes, and we can set len as $$len=s\cdot\left(\frac{nv}{k\cdot s}\right)=\frac{nv}{k}$$ 

The value len indicates the number of blocks that can be stored in Loc. After determining the length, the value sa is set by the number of blocks in the updated stripe (denoted nu) that are contained within Loc = [sa, sa + len − 1]. We hope that Loc can contain more blocks in the updated stripe to reduce the additional disk I/Os. $$\text{Maximize }nu\text{ in }[sa,sa+len-1]$$ 

To this end, Alg. 3 conducts reasonable migration of the blocks in the recycled and updated stripes for each node. It first merges the stripe pair (Sx,Sy) (e.g., Sx → Sy) that invalid data blocks in Sy are in Loc. If the invalid data block by,i in updated stripe Sy is in Loc, it migrates the valid data blocks bx,i in Sx to by,i (Lines 4-5); If the invalid data blocks bx,i in recycled stripe Sx is in Loc and the valid data blocks by,i in updated stripe Sy is not in Loc, it migrates the valid data blocks by,i in Sy to bx,i (Lines 6-7); After the above-mentioned migration is completed, the storage space of some blocks from Sx can be released to further complete the subsequent migration. Then, it next merges the stripe pair (Sx,Sy) that Sx and Sy are not in Loc (Lines 8-14). For each (Sx,Sy), it obtains the free fragment location floc from Loc, which means that filling floc can reduce the number of discontinuous fragments and move valid data blocks of Sx and all blocks of Sy to floc. Since the valid data blocks in all recycled stripes and invalid data and parity blocks in all updated stripes require read/write operations to complete the parity updates (Sec. IV-C), Alg. 3 only needs additional disk I/Os operations of valid data blocks for these updated stripes that are not in Loc. It also allocates appropriate spaces to store the updated stripes, thus eliminating the fragments at the cost of limited disk I/Os. 

An Example: Fig. 9(a) shows the naive merging, and it causes three discontinuous fragments. In Fig. 8(a), nv = 12 and hence len = 12 4 = 3. When sa = 1, Loc can contain the most blocks in updated stripes (e.g., S2 and S3), thus Loc = [1,3] for all nodes. Fig. 9(b) shows the merging by Alg. 3. For N1, b5,1(∉ Loc) in updated stripe S5 is valid data block. It obtains the free storage space floc = 1 from Loc and additionally moves b5,1 to b1,1. For N2, b4,2(∉ Loc) in recycled stripe S4 is valid data block. It obtains the free storage space floc = 1 from Loc and additionally moves b4,2 to b2,1. For N3, b1,3(∈ Loc) in recycled stripe S1 is valid data block, b3,3(∈ Loc) in updated stripe S3 is invalid data block. It can moves b1,3 to b3,3. The migration process of other nodes is similar to the above. Thus, Alg. 3 only causes one fragment in Fig. 9(b). 

Time Complexity: Alg. 3 traverses at most s pairs in Solu. Finding the floc in Line 10 and 13 takes O($nv/k$) time. Therefore, the time complexity of Alg. 3 is O($n\cdot s\cdot nv/k$).

如观察 2 所述，释放的空间分散在磁盘上，写入新数据时会带来额外的磁盘寻道。例如，图 8(b) 的合并方案执行后会产生图 9(a) 中的 3 处碎片。一种简单做法是移动 $S_5$ 中所有块以填满 $S_1$ 的空闲空间，消除碎片；但这仍会额外产生 12 次磁盘 I/O（即读取并写入 6 个块）。处理大量条带时，这种做法会消耗总线带宽资源，进而干扰前台任务。为此，我们设计了算法 3，其核心思想是在合并期间谨慎地将块迁移到预定的连续存储空间；也就是说，应当避免在合并条带时产生新的碎片。

**算法 3：消除碎片空间。**

输入：合并方案 $Solu$

```text
1  对每个节点 N_i 执行
2      为 N_i 预定存储位置 Loc
3      对 Solu 中每对 (S_x, S_y) 执行
4          若 b_{x,i} 为有效数据、b_{y,i}(∈ Loc) 为无效数据，则
5              将 b_{x,i} 迁移至 b_{y,i}
6          若 b_{x,i}(∈ Loc) 为无效数据、b_{y,i}(∉ Loc) 为有效数据，则
7              将 b_{y,i} 迁移至 b_{x,i}
8      对 Solu 中每对 (S_x, S_y) 执行
9          若 b_{x,i}(∉ Loc) 为有效数据、b_{y,i}(∉ Loc) 为无效数据，则
10             从 Loc 获取空闲存储空间 floc
11             将 b_{x,i} 迁移至 b_{y,floc}
12         若 b_{y,i}(∉ Loc) 为有效数据或校验块，则
13             从 Loc 获取空闲存储空间 floc
14             将 b_{y,i} 迁移至 b_{y,floc}
```

图 9. 对图 8(b) 的合并方案消除碎片的示例。

**算法细节：**算法 3 需要为每个节点 $N_i$ 预定一个连续存储位置 $Loc$，其中包含长度 $len$ 与起始地址 $sa$。设 $nv$ 是 $s$ 个条带中的有效数据块数量，可以将 $len$ 设为：
$$len=s\cdot\left(\frac{nv}{k\cdot s}\right)=\frac{nv}{k}$$

$len$ 表示 $Loc$ 中可存储的块数。确定长度后，根据 $Loc=[sa,sa+len-1]$ 中包含的更新条带块数（记为 $nu$）来设置 $sa$。我们希望 $Loc$ 包含更多更新条带中的块，以减少额外磁盘 I/O。
$$\text{Maximize }nu\text{ in }[sa,sa+len-1]$$

为此，算法 3 在每个节点上对回收条带和更新条带中的块进行适当迁移。它首先合并无效数据块位于 $Loc$ 内的条带对 $(S_x,S_y)$（例如 $S_x\rightarrow S_y$）。如果更新条带 $S_y$ 中的无效数据块 $b_{y,i}$ 位于 $Loc$，就将 $S_x$ 中的有效数据块 $b_{x,i}$ 迁移至 $b_{y,i}$（第 4–5 行）；如果回收条带 $S_x$ 中的无效数据块 $b_{x,i}$ 位于 $Loc$，而更新条带 $S_y$ 中的有效数据块 $b_{y,i}$ 不在 $Loc$，则将 $b_{y,i}$ 迁移至 $b_{x,i}$（第 6–7 行）。完成上述迁移后，$S_x$ 中一些块所占用的存储空间可以释放，从而进行后续迁移。接着，它合并 $S_x$ 和 $S_y$ 均不在 $Loc$ 内的条带对 $(S_x,S_y)$（第 8–14 行）。对于每一对 $(S_x,S_y)$，算法从 $Loc$ 中取得空闲碎片位置 $floc$；填充该位置可以减少不连续碎片的数量，然后把 $S_x$ 中的有效数据块和 $S_y$ 中的所有块迁移到 $floc$。由于所有回收条带中的有效数据块，以及所有更新条带中的无效数据块和校验块，在完成校验更新时都需要读写操作（第 IV-C 节），算法 3 只需要对不在 $Loc$ 中的更新条带的有效数据块执行额外磁盘 I/O。它也为更新条带分配适当空间，因此只需有限的磁盘 I/O 代价就能消除碎片。

**示例：**图 9(a) 给出简单合并的结果，产生了三处不连续的碎片。在图 8(a) 中，$nv=12$，因此 $len=12/4=3$。当 $sa=1$ 时，$Loc$ 能容纳更新条带（例如 $S_2$ 和 $S_3$）中的最多块，所以所有节点的 $Loc=[1,3]$。图 9(b) 给出算法 3 的合并结果。对 $N_1$ 而言，更新条带 $S_5$ 中的 $b_{5,1}(
otin Loc)$ 是有效数据块。算法从 $Loc$ 取得空闲存储位置 $floc=1$，并额外把 $b_{5,1}$ 迁移到 $b_{1,1}$。对 $N_2$ 而言，回收条带 $S_4$ 中的 $b_{4,2}(
otin Loc)$ 是有效数据块。算法从 $Loc$ 取得空闲位置 $floc=1$，并额外把 $b_{4,2}$ 迁移到 $b_{2,1}$。对 $N_3$ 而言，回收条带 $S_1$ 中的 $b_{1,3}(\in Loc)$ 是有效数据块，更新条带 $S_3$ 中的 $b_{3,3}(\in Loc)$ 是无效数据块，可以把 $b_{1,3}$ 迁移到 $b_{3,3}$。其他节点的迁移过程与之类似。因此，算法 3 在图 9(b) 中仅产生一处碎片。

**时间复杂度：**算法 3 最多遍历 $Solu$ 中的 $s$ 对条带。在第 10、13 行寻找 $floc$ 耗时 $O(nv/k)$。因此，算法 3 的时间复杂度为 $O(n\cdot s\cdot nv/k)$。

sections.title: C. Balancing Traffic Load
sections.originalMarkdown:
After substituting the invalid data blocks with valid ones, the parity blocks in updated stripes must be updated. Here, we adopt the latest update scheme, RackCU [9], that can minimize the single-stripe network traffic to update parity blocks. However, based on the above Observation 3, the random selection of collectors for multi-stripe updates may cause unbalanced network traffic across nodes, further prolonging the GC process. Our main idea is to iteratively alleviate the network traffic on the most traffic-loaded node by substituting the selected collectors with its alternatives. We also selectively schedule the update transmission links via the maximum flow algorithm to saturate the bandwidth utilization. 

**Algorithm 4: Balancing Traffic Load.**

Input: a merge solution $Solu$

```text
1  Coll = ∅
2  for each (S_x, S_y) in Solu do
3      Randomly select one block b_{y,c} from S_y as the collector
4      Coll += (S_y, b_{y,c})
5  while each optimization do
6      l = compute load rate of Coll
7      for each (S_y, b_{y,c}) in Coll do
8          for each updated data and parity block b_{y,c′} in S_y do
9              nColl = Coll - (S_y, b_{y,c}) + (S_y, b_{y,c′})
10             nl = compute load rate of nColl
11             if nl < l then
12                 Coll = nColl
13                 Jump to the next while-loop in Line 5
14 Exit the while-loop in Line 5 if Coll does not change
15 Schedule the updating transmission in Coll via the maximum flow algorithm
```

Fig. 10. Example of balancing traffic load and scheduling update transmission for the merge solution of Fig. 9(b).

Algorithm Details: Algorithm 4 first randomly selects one collector block by,c for each updated stripe Sy to initialize the set Coll (Lines 2-4). It then adopts the greedy idea to iteratively optimize the Coll and reduce the load rate (Lines 5-13). Specifically, Alg. 4 uses l to record the current load rate of Coll (Line 6). For each (Sy,by,c) in Coll, it tries all updated data and parity blocks by,c0 in Sy to substitute the current collector by,c, generates the new set nColl, and computes the load rate nl of nColl (Lines 7-10). If the new nColl has a lower load rate (nl < l), Alg. 4 substitutes Coll with nColl and jumps to the while-loop in Line 5 to start the next optimization (Lines 11-13). The load rate monotonically decreases for each optimization, and Alg. 4 repeats the above optimization until there is no substitution in Coll (Line 14). 

After determining the collectors, we selectively schedule the transmission routing for parity updates (Line 15). Suppose that a block can be transmitted across a network link in a timeslot [7], [8]. To avoid network congestion, a node can send and receive one block in a timeslot. Since each collector needs to collect multiple data deltas from updated blocks and update multiple parity blocks, each stripe requires multiple timeslots to complete the updates. For multi-stripe updates, we formulate the scheduling as a maximum flow problem [24] that aims to complete more links transmission at each timeslot. We first construct a bipartite graph with n sending nodes and n receiving nodes and then add an edge in the graph if a node needs to send one block to the receiving node. We can use the Edmonds-Karp algorithm [25] to find a maximum flow that completes the most links transmissions in each timeslot. We repeat the algorithm until all links are transmitted. 

An Example: Fig. 10(a) and 10(b) shows an example of balancing traffic load for the merge solution of Fig. 9(b). For random collector selection in Fig. 10(a), the N4 uploads the most four blocks, and the load rate is LR = $4/((2+1+4)/6)=24/7$. After optimization by Alg. 4, the most network traffic is two in Fig. 10(b), and the load rate is LR = $2/((2+2+2+1)/6)=12/7$. Then, Alg. 4 begin to schedule the transmission links. Here, we only show the transmission in the first timeslot in Fig. 10(c). The first timeslot in Fig. 10(b) has four links: N2 → N3 for S1, N4 → N2 for S2, and N3=N4 → N5 for S3. If we schedule the link N2 → N3 for S1 and N4 → N5 for S3, only two links are completed in this timeslot. By the above maximum flow algorithm, it can schedule three links in this timeslot by delaying the transmission of link N4 → N5 for S3. 

Time Complexity: We finally analyze the time complexity of Alg. 4. Alg. 4 traverses at most s pairs to initialize Coll. Each optimization takes O(k + m) to adjust the collector for each stripe. Suppose that t is the round of optimization, and balancing the traffic load takes O(t · s · (k + m)). If there are n nodes and e edges in the network, the complexity of the Edmonds-Karp algorithm is O(n · e² ). Therefore, the time complexity of Alg. 4 is O(s + t · s · (k + m) + n · e² ) ≈ O(t · s · (k + m) + n · e² ).

**算法 4：平衡流量负载。**

输入：合并方案 $Solu$


**算法细节：**算法 4 首先为每个更新条带 $S_y$ 随机选择一个收集块 $b_{y,c}$，初始化集合 $Coll$（第 2–4 行）。随后采用贪心方法，迭代优化 $Coll$ 并降低负载率（第 5–13 行）。具体而言，算法 4 使用 $l$ 记录 $Coll$ 当前的负载率（第 6 行）。对于 $Coll$ 中每个 $(S_y,b_{y,c})$，它尝试用 $S_y$ 中所有更新数据块和校验块 $b_{y,c'}$ 替换当前收集块 $b_{y,c}$，形成新集合 $nColl$，并计算其负载率 $nl$（第 7–10 行）。如果新集合的负载率更低（$nl<l$），算法 4 就以 $nColl$ 替换 $Coll$，并跳转到第 5 行的 while 循环，开始下一轮优化（第 11–13 行）。每轮优化的负载率都单调下降，算法 4 重复这一过程，直到 $Coll$ 中不再发生替换（第 14 行）。

确定收集块后，我们有选择地调度校验更新的传输路径（第 15 行）。假设一个块可以在一个时隙内通过一条网络链路传输 [7]、[8]。为避免网络拥塞，一个节点可以在一个时隙中发送和接收一个块。由于每个收集块需要从更新块收集多个数据增量并更新多个校验块，每个条带都需要多个时隙才能完成更新。对于多条带更新，我们将调度建模为最大流问题 [24]，目标是在每个时隙内完成更多链路传输。首先构造包含 $n$ 个发送节点和 $n$ 个接收节点的二分图；如果一个节点需要向某个接收节点发送一个块，就在图中添加一条边。可以使用 Edmonds–Karp 算法 [25] 寻找最大流，使每个时隙完成最多的链路传输。反复执行该算法，直到所有链路均完成传输。

**示例：**图 10(a) 和图 10(b) 展示了对图 9(b) 的合并方案平衡流量负载的例子。图 10(a) 中随机选择收集块后，$N_4$ 的上传量最大，为 4 个块，负载率为 $LR=4/((2+1+4)/6)=24/7$。经算法 4 优化，图 10(b) 中最大的网络流量为 2，负载率为 $LR=2/((2+2+2+1)/6)=12/7$。然后，算法 4 开始调度传输链路。这里仅在图 10(c) 中展示第一个时隙的传输。图 10(b) 中，第一个时隙有四条链路：$S_1$ 的 $N_2\rightarrow N_3$、$S_2$ 的 $N_4\rightarrow N_2$，以及 $S_3$ 的 $N_3/N_4\rightarrow N_5$。若调度 $S_1$ 的 $N_2\rightarrow N_3$ 和 $S_3$ 的 $N_4\rightarrow N_5$，该时隙仅能完成两条链路。借助上述最大流算法，推迟 $S_3$ 的 $N_4\rightarrow N_5$ 传输后，该时隙可以调度三条链路。

**时间复杂度：**最后分析算法 4 的时间复杂度。算法 4 最多遍历 $s$ 个条带对来初始化 $Coll$。每轮优化对每个条带调整收集块需要 $O(k+m)$ 时间。设优化轮数为 $t$，平衡流量负载需要 $O(t\cdot s\cdot(k+m))$ 时间。如果网络中有 $n$ 个节点、$e$ 条边，Edmonds–Karp 算法的复杂度为 $O(n\cdot e^2)$。因此，算法 4 的时间复杂度为 $O(s+t\cdot s\cdot(k+m)+n\cdot e^2)\approx O(t\cdot s\cdot(k+m)+n\cdot e^2)$。

sections.title: D. Discussion
sections.originalMarkdown:
Extensions: This section will discuss the possible extensions of FastGC. We show that FastGC can be easily extended to solve the GC problems in LRC-based and large-scale clusters. 

GC in LRC-based clusters: Today’s storage clusters often adopt LRC code [1] (used in Azure cloud storage) to maintain high data reliability. An LRC(k, l, g) code encodes k data blocks into g global parity blocks and generates a local parity block per k/l data blocks. As an orthogonal method, FastGC can be effortlessly extended to LRC code. FastGC generates the merge solution based on the layout of data blocks, similar to that of RS code, and greedily schedules the transmission routing for each local and global parity update. 

GC in large-scale clusters: A cluster may have a tremendous number of stripes [26], and recycling these stripes simultaneously is usually not preferable, as it easily overloads the network and storage I/Os of the clustered storage system. Therefore, we can divide a large number of stripes into smaller groups based on the current system resource usage and required resources for each group. FastGC batch-processes multiple groups to complete the GC of the whole cluster. 

Limitations: The current FastGC has limitations in regenerating code clusters and partially invalid scenarios, and it does not take into account the rack architecture of the cluster. We consider these limitations as future work. 

GC for regenerating code: The regenerating code (RC) [27], [28] divides each block into multiple sub-blocks, and different sub-blocks are combined to generate parity blocks. To recycle the invalid blocks for RC, FastGC needs to manage more complex metadata, increasing the running time, metadata management costs, and memory overhead. Due to the wide use of RS code (HDFS [2], QFS [19], and Ceph [17]) and LRC code (Microsoft Azure Storage [1]) in current storage systems, FastGC is designed to improve the recovery performance for the two most popular codes. How to efficiently extend FastGC to solve the garbage collection issues in RC-based storage clusters will be important work for us in the future. 

GC for partially invalid scenarios: When some data in a block becomes invalid, such a situation is referred to as a partially invalid scenario. We present the following solution. Data migration is carried out within each node. The data blocks within the node are sorted in descending order of valid data amount. The valid data in the block with the least amount of valid data is migrated to the block with the largest amount of valid data. The invalid data in some blocks needs to be temporarily stored and released after the parity update is completed. Therefore, partially invalid scenarios can be transformed into the scenarios described in this paper, and FastGC can be used to complete the GC. The migration process only occurs within the node and will not cause any network traffic across nodes. In addition, the sorting operation can minimize the inter-disk traffic generated by the migration. Since the transmission rate between disks is usually much higher than that between nodes, the data migration within the node will not have a significant impact on the performance. 

GC for rack architecture: FastGC assumes that all nodes reside in a single rack. However, modern erasure-coded storage clusters usually organize nodes in multiple racks, and the available cross-rack bandwidth resources are typically lower than the intra-rack bandwidth resources [8], [29]. Thus, we need to find an appropriate merge solution that can complete the GC process within racks as much as possible to reduce the cross-rack network traffic. In addition, updating multiple stripes concurrently may also introduce imbalanced traffic loads between racks, further affecting GC efficiency.

**扩展：**本节讨论 FastGC 可能的扩展。我们说明，FastGC 可以容易地扩展，用于解决基于 LRC 的集群和大规模集群中的 GC 问题。

**基于 LRC 的集群中的 GC：**如今，存储集群常采用 LRC 码 [1]（Azure 云存储使用该编码）来保持高数据可靠性。LRC$(k,l,g)$ 将 $k$ 个数据块编码为 $g$ 个全局校验块，并针对每 $k/l$ 个数据块生成一个局部校验块。FastGC 与编码方法正交，因此可以直接扩展到 LRC 码。与 RS 码类似，FastGC 根据数据块布局生成合并方案，并贪心调度每次局部及全局校验更新的传输路径。

**大规模集群中的 GC：**集群可能含有大量条带 [26]，同时回收这些条带通常不可取，因为这容易使集群存储系统的网络和存储 I/O 过载。因此，可依据当前系统资源使用情况以及每组所需资源，将大量条带划分为更小的组。FastGC 分批处理多组条带，完成整个集群的 GC。

**局限性：**当前的 FastGC 在再生码集群及块部分失效的场景中存在局限，并且没有考虑集群的机架结构。我们将这些局限留待未来研究。

**再生码的 GC：**再生码（RC）[27]、[28] 将每个块划分为多个子块，再将不同子块组合生成校验块。要回收 RC 中的无效块，FastGC 必须管理更复杂的元数据，从而增加运行时间、元数据管理成本和内存开销。鉴于当前存储系统广泛使用 RS 码（HDFS [2]、QFS [19] 和 Ceph [17]）以及 LRC 码（Microsoft Azure Storage [1]），FastGC 的设计目标是改善这两种最常用编码下的恢复性能。未来一项重要工作是高效扩展 FastGC，以解决基于 RC 的存储集群中的垃圾回收问题。

**块部分失效场景中的 GC：**当一个块中的部分数据失效，就称为块部分失效场景。我们提出如下解决方案：在每个节点内部执行数据迁移。按有效数据量降序排列节点中的数据块，将有效数据量最少的块中的有效数据迁移到有效数据量最多的块中。部分块里的无效数据需要暂时保留，并在校验更新完成后释放。这样，就能将块部分失效场景转换为本文描述的场景，并使用 FastGC 完成 GC。迁移仅在节点内部发生，不会造成跨节点网络流量。此外，排序操作可以最小化迁移产生的跨磁盘流量。由于磁盘间的传输速率通常远高于节点间的传输速率，节点内数据迁移不会对性能造成显著影响。

**机架结构下的 GC：**FastGC 假设所有节点位于同一个机架。然而，现代纠删码存储集群通常把节点组织在多个机架上，且可用的跨机架带宽资源通常小于机架内带宽资源 [8]、[29]。因此，需要找到适当的合并方案，尽可能在机架内完成 GC，以减少跨机架网络流量。此外，并发更新多个条带也可能造成机架间流量负载不平衡，进一步影响 GC 效率。

sections.title: V. IMPLEMENTATION
sections.originalMarkdown:
**System Architecture.** We implemented a FastGC prototype in C++ with 4,700 lines of code (LoC). Fig. 11 presents the system architecture of the prototype, which comprises a global coordinator and multiple storage nodes. The coordinator stores the cluster metadata (e.g., the node, stripe, and block IDs) and organizes the GC process by GC module. When the GC is triggered, it generates the merge solution, allocates the storage space to the new stripes, and balances network traffic across nodes. The coordinator issues the above commands to all nodes. Upon receiving the commands, each node migrates and updates the blocks to complete the GC process.

*Fig. 11. System architecture of FastGC.*

**Implementation Details.** FastGC adopts three third-party libraries for efficient encoding operations, including (i) Jerasure [30] and GF-complete [31], which implement the Galois-Field operations of RS codes, and (ii) Redis [32], which maintains an in-memory key-value store for internal communications and block transmissions. We argue that FastGC can be treated as an independent component in storage clusters to guide the GC process. We also implement GOOD [13] and BCStore [16] in the same system for fair comparisons.

**Traces Replay.** We use YCSB [33] to generate a representative workload to evaluate FastGC. The workload has a 50%:50% read/update ratio and follows the Zipfian distribution (with an alpha value of 0.99 by default) to mimic the popularity distribution. The size of the value of an object is set as 1024 KiB [9], and we consider each object as a data block for simplicity. When replaying a workload, we identify the block IDs to be updated and adopt the out-of-place update manner, and the old data block is considered invalid. This trace-replay method is also used in [9], [16]. We further trigger the GC process based on a new metric called trigger rate, and it can be calculated as

$$\text{trigger rate} = \frac{\text{the number of invalid data blocks}}{s \cdot k}$$

When the rate reaches a predetermined threshold (e.g., 0.4), the GC process is triggered to recycle the invalid spaces [13].

sections.title: VI. EVALUATION
sections.originalMarkdown:
We comprehensively evaluate FastGC from large-scale simulation and real-cloud Alibaba ECS experiments. We expect to answer the following questions.

- Can FastGC effectively reduce and balance the network traffic, and is FastGC extensible? (Experiment A.1-A.4)
- How do the three designed algorithms of FastGC (Alg. 1 to 3) affect the computation time and GC time? (Experiment B.1-B.2)
- How much GC time can FastGC reduce when any cluster configuration varies? (Experiment B.3-B.5)
- Will FastGC sustain read/write performance effectiveness after GC in real-cloud clusters? (Experiment B.6-B.7)

sections.title: A. Large-Scale Simulation
sections.originalMarkdown:
We remove the actual storage and transmission from our prototype and first conduct the large-scale simulation to measure the network traffic GT and load rate of cluster LR. We deploy the simulator on a server equipped with Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6230 CPU @ 2.10GHz, 256 GB RAM, and 2 TB solid state hard disk. The server runs on Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS. We adopt the following default configurations. We generate s = 1000 stripes that are encoded by RS(k = 10, m = 4) (used in Hadoop HDFS [2]) and evenly disperse them across n = 20 nodes while ensuring the node-level fault tolerance. The block size is 1MB, and the trigger rate is 0.4 by default. We repeat each test for 5 runs and show the average values, and the maximum and minimum values in the figures.

**Experiment A.1 (Impact of coding parameters).** We first study the impact of different coding parameters, including (6, 3) (used in QFS [19]), (10, 4) (consistent with Hadoop HDFS [2]), and (12, 4) (deployed in Azure [1]). We make three key observations from the results in Fig. 12. First, the network traffic of all three methods increases when facing larger k and m. This is because when parameters increase, more data blocks are re-encoded, and more parity blocks are needed to be updated, thereby adding more transmission traffic. Second, FastGC achieves the least network traffic for all methods and reduces the traffic by 63.20%-81.22% and 10.36%-24.19% on average compared to GOOD and BCStore, respectively. The rationale is that FastGC reduces the network traffic by carefully selecting merged stripe pairs. Third, FastGC significantly balances the upload and download network traffic across nodes. The average load rate of FastGC across all the tests is 1.09, which closely approaches the optimum value 1. However, We can also find that because of the negligence of the unbalanced network traffic, the average load rate of GOOD and BCStore is 1.51 and 1.27. Although the efficacy of FastGC on traffic reduction recedes when facing smaller k and m, we will show that the unbalanced network traffic still prolongs the GC time in Sec. VI-B.

*Fig. 12. Experiment A.1 (Impact of coding parameters).*

**Experiment A.2 (Impact of number of nodes).** We next study how different numbers of nodes influence the GC. We use different numbers of nodes, including n = 15, 20, 25. Fig. 13 depicts the results. Fig. 13(a) shows that FastGC can reduce 65.39% and 22.16% of network traffic on average compared to GOOD and BCStore, respectively. FastGC retains its efficacy in balancing the inter-node upload and download network traffic for different numbers of nodes. Overall, in Fig. 13(b), the average load rates of GOOD, BCStore, and FastGC are 1.50, 1.23, and 1.1, respectively. Experiments have also proved that FastGC can still work well and is much more stable than the other two methods under different cluster configurations.

*Fig. 13. Experiment A.2 (Impact of number of nodes).*

**Experiment A.3 (Impact of number of stripes).** We further study the impact of the number of stripes from s = 500 to s = 2000. As shown in Fig. 14(a), we observe that the network traffic increases with the number of stripes. The underlying reason is that the GC of more stripes requires transferring more data blocks and updating more parity blocks. Besides, the larger number of stripes enhances the effectiveness of FastGC on traffic reduction. For example, compared to BCStore, the traffic reduction ratio of FastGC is 18.97% for s = 500 stripes, while the ratio increases to 24.42% for s = 2000 stripes. The reason is that the larger s will increase the opportunity to find the optimal merging from the optimization room for FastGC. As shown in Fig. 14(b), the number of stripes has a marginal impact on the resulting load rate of the cluster, and FastGC can maintain an effective load balancing.

*Fig. 14. Experiment A.3 (Impact of number of stripes).*

**Experiment A.4 (Impact of LRC code).** We finally evaluate the scalability of FastGC for LRC code. We select LRC(6, 2, 2), LRC(8, 2, 2), and LRC(10, 2, 4) for evaluation, and these codes are considered in previous work [10]. Fig. 15 shows that FastGC can still retain its efficacy and reduce the network traffic for different LRC codes; it also significantly balances the inter-node traffic compared to GOOD and BCStore. Experiments also have demonstrated that FastGC can be easily applied to other erasure codes as a complementary method.

*Fig. 15. Experiment A.4 (Impact of LRC code).*

我们从原型中移除实际的存储和传输操作，首先开展大规模模拟实验，测量网络流量 GT 和集群负载率 LR。模拟器部署在一台配备 Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6230 CPU @ 2.10GHz、256 GB 内存和 2 TB 固态硬盘的服务器上，运行 Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS。我们采用以下默认配置：生成 s = 1000 个由 RS(k = 10, m = 4) 编码的条带（Hadoop HDFS [2] 使用该配置），将它们均匀分散在 n = 20 个节点上，同时保证节点级容错。数据块大小为 1MB，默认触发率为 0.4。每组测试重复运行 5 次，并在图中展示平均值、最大值和最小值。

**实验 A.1（编码参数的影响）。** 我们首先研究不同编码参数的影响，包括 (6, 3)（QFS [19] 使用）、(10, 4)（与 Hadoop HDFS [2] 一致）和 (12, 4)（Azure [1] 部署）。从图 12 的结果中，我们得到三个主要观察。第一，当 k 和 m 增大时，三种方法的网络流量都会增加。这是因为参数增大后，需要重新编码更多数据块，并更新更多校验块，从而增加传输流量。第二，FastGC 在所有方法中产生的网络流量最少，与 GOOD 和 BCStore 相比，平均分别减少 63.20%-81.22% 和 10.36%-24.19% 的流量。原因是 FastGC 通过精心选择要合并的条带对来减少网络流量。第三，FastGC 显著平衡了各节点的上传和下载网络流量。在所有测试中，FastGC 的平均负载率为 1.09，十分接近最优值 1。但我们也可以发现，由于 GOOD 和 BCStore 忽略了网络流量不均衡的问题，其平均负载率分别为 1.51 和 1.27。尽管当 k 和 m 较小时，FastGC 减少流量的效果会减弱，但我们将在第 VI-B 节说明，网络流量不均衡仍会延长 GC 时间。

*图 12. 实验 A.1（编码参数的影响）。*

**实验 A.2（节点数量的影响）。** 接下来，我们研究不同节点数量如何影响 GC。我们分别使用 n = 15、20、25 个节点。图 13 展示了结果。图 13(a) 表明，与 GOOD 和 BCStore 相比，FastGC 平均分别减少 65.39% 和 22.16% 的网络流量。对于不同的节点数量，FastGC 仍能有效平衡节点间的上传和下载网络流量。总体而言，在图 13(b) 中，GOOD、BCStore 和 FastGC 的平均负载率分别为 1.50、1.23 和 1.1。实验还证明，在不同集群配置下，FastGC 依然能够良好运行，且比另外两种方法稳定得多。

*图 13. 实验 A.2（节点数量的影响）。*

**实验 A.3（条带数量的影响）。** 我们进一步研究条带数量从 s = 500 变化到 s = 2000 时的影响。如图 14(a) 所示，网络流量随条带数量增加而增加。原因在于，回收更多条带需要传输更多数据块并更新更多校验块。此外，条带数量越多，FastGC 减少流量的效果越明显。例如，与 BCStore 相比，s = 500 时 FastGC 的流量减少比例为 18.97%，而 s = 2000 时上升至 24.42%。这是因为较大的 s 扩大了 FastGC 的优化空间，增加了找到最优合并方案的机会。如图 14(b) 所示，条带数量对最终的集群负载率影响很小，FastGC 能够保持有效的负载均衡。

*图 14. 实验 A.3（条带数量的影响）。*

**实验 A.4（LRC 码的影响）。** 最后，我们评估 FastGC 对 LRC 码的可扩展性。我们选取 LRC(6, 2, 2)、LRC(8, 2, 2) 和 LRC(10, 2, 4) 进行评估，这些编码也曾在已有工作 [10] 中使用。图 15 表明，对于不同的 LRC 码，FastGC 仍能保持效果并减少网络流量；与 GOOD 和 BCStore 相比，它也显著平衡了节点间流量。实验还表明，FastGC 可以轻松作为一种互补方法应用于其他纠删码。

*图 15. 实验 A.4（LRC 码的影响）。*

We next conduct real-cloud Alibaba ECS [34] experiments with 15 ecs.d1.2xlarge instances as one coordinator and 14 storage nodes to evaluate the performance of FastGC in a real-world cloud environment. Each instance is equipped with 8 vCPUs, 32 GB RAM, and 4 × 5905 GB SATA HDDs. The operating system is Ubuntu 16.04, and the network bandwidth is around 3Gbps (measured by iperf [35]). We also select RS(10, 4), set the block size as 1MB, fix the number of stripes as 1000, and configure the trigger rate as 0.4. We measure the computation time, GC time, disk I/Os, and read/write throughput after GC. We also report the average results of each experiment over five runs and show the average, maximum, and minimum values.

**Experiment B.1 (Computation analysis of FastGC).** We first evaluate the computation time to establish the merge solution for FastGC and compare it with BCStore (black Y axis of Fig. 16). To quantify the GC cost, we also measure the GC time (including the computation time) and report the ratio of computation time to GC time (red Y axis of Fig. 16). We use different numbers of stripes (s = 100 to 10000) and vary the code parameters (k, m) by using different settings: RS(4, 2) , RS(6, 3), and RS(10, 4). Fig. 16 shows the results. We can see that the computation time of BCStore and FastGC gradually increases with the number of stripes and the code parameters. Specifically, BCStore only needs 0.21 seconds at most to generate the solution, and FastGC takes more time (e.g., 2.08 seconds) to compute. The result is consistent with their time complexities, e.g., O(s · log s) for BCStore. In addition, the computation time only occupies 0.08%-2.31% of the GC time, and the computation time of merge solution will not significantly increase the GC time. Therefore, we argue that FastGC is extremely efficient in finding the solution. FastGC is qualified to be deployed in large-scale clusters with tremendous stripes.

*Fig. 16. Experiment B.1 (Computation analysis of FastGC).*

**Experiment B.2 (Breakdown analysis of FastGC).** We further conduct the breakdown analysis of FastGC and investigate the effectiveness of each designed algorithm. For simplicity, we abbreviate the algorithms of FastGC as follows: (i) generating merge solution (GMS), which finds an efficient merge solution to reduce the network traffic (Alg. 1 and 2 in Sec. IV-A) and randomly selects a collector for each updated stripe, and (ii) balancing traffic load (BTL), which randomly selects two non-full stripes that can be merged into a full stripe and greedily selects a collector for each updated stripe (Alg. 4 in Sec. IV-C). Hence, FastGC is the synthesis of GMS+BTL, and Fig. 17 illustrates the results. We observe that BTL is more effective than GMS, and finding the efficient merge solution can reduce more GC time than balancing the traffic load. Compared with GOOD and BCStore, GMS can reduce GC time by 6.25%-52.13%, while BTL is only 18.75%-59.38%. Moreover, we also observe that FastGC has the lowest GC time among all the methods, which indicates that the two algorithms are complementary and do not compromise the effectiveness.

*Fig. 17. Experiment B.2 (Breakdown analysis of FastGC).*

**Experiment B.3 (Impact of network bandwidth).** Next, we study the impact of network bandwidth, which varies as 0.5Gbps, 1Gbps, and 3Gbps (the default bandwidth). The bandwidth of each instance is throttled by the Wondershaper tool [37], and Fig. 18(a) shows the GC time of all methods. We can see that the three methods showcase a similar trend, and the GC time gradually decreases with the network bandwidth, showing that the GC process is restricted by the network bandwidth and revealing the necessity of reducing network traffic in a scarce bandwidth environment. Overall, FastGC can reduce the GC time by 63.95-72.36% and 34.25-42.60% compared to GOOD and BCStore, respectively.

**Experiment B.4 (Impact of trigger rate).** We vary the trigger rate (Defined in Sec. V) from 0.2 to 0.6 and measure the resulting GC time. Fig. 18(b) shows that FastGC reduces the GC time by 57.19% and 33.95% on average across different trigger rates, compared to GOOD and BCStore, respectively. Consequently, when the trigger rate is 0.2, the efficacy of FastGC recedes. We suspect that the solution room becomes smaller as the trigger rate decreases, and finding an efficient merge solution for FastGC is more difficult.

*Fig. 18. Impact of the cluster configurations.*

**Experiment B.5 (Impact of workload settings).** We next consider different request distributions for workloads and compare GOOD, BCStore, and FastGC in terms of GC time. The YCSB workload adopts three different distributions (the uniform distribution, the Zipfian distribution with an alpha value of 0.99, and the hotspot distribution) to generate update requests. We also simulate a workload to generate deletion requests and employ both uniform and normal distributions. Fig. 19 shows the results. We observe that the more dispersed the request distribution is, the more effective FastGC is in reducing the GC time. For example, compared to BCStore, the GC time reduction ratio of FastGC is 7.69% in the YCSB workload for the hotspot distribution, while the ratio increases to 35.93% for the uniform distribution. The workload for generating deletion requests also shows similar results. The main reason is that the more dispersed the distribution of requests is, the more dispersed the invalid data will be, which will provide greater optimization space in FastGC.

*Fig. 19. Experiment B.5 (Impact of workload settings).*

**Experiment B.6 (Disk I/Os analysis).** In Sec. III-A, we argue that releasing the recycled stripes will introduce fragment spaces, which affects the write performance after GC. Although we can greedily move the updated stripes to eliminate the discontinuous fragments (Called Naive), it still causes significant disk I/Os. To show the advantages of Alg. 3, we measure the total disk I/Os with and without Naive for three methods, with and without Alg. 3 for FastGC. As shown in Fig. 20(a), BCStore has the least disk I/Os when the fragment spaces are not eliminated. The reason is that BCStore migrates the valid blocks from the stripes with the most invalid blocks to those with the least invalid blocks, thus minimizing the disk I/Os. Further, in Fig. 20(b), the naive eliminating strategy increases 8.3%, 79.6%, and 51.76% disk I/Os for GOOD, BCStore, and FastGC without Alg. 3. As a comparison, FastGC only adds 23.21% disk I/Os compared to no Alg. 3 and has the least disk I/Os.

*Fig. 20. Experiment B.6 (Disk I/Os analysis).*

**Experiment B.7 (Read/Write performance after GC).** We finally measure the read and write throughput after GC. We adopt ecs.d1.2xlarge instances and configure four SATA HDD with for each instance. We also measure the baseline read performance by keeping the old valid block distribution without the GC process and baseline write performance by writing the new data to continuous spaces. Fig. 21(a) shows that GOOD and FastGC have similar read throughput, and the differences between FastGC and the baseline are very small (within 3.54%). In contrast, BCStore is the worst among all methods since it performs the GC process at the granularity of blocks instead of stripes, and some valid data blocks belonging to the same stripe may concentrate on a few nodes. In Fig. 21(b), FastGC has almost the same write throughput as baseline, and the write throughput of GOOD and BCStore decreased by 5.26% and 21.05%, respectively. It also reveals the necessity of eliminating the discontinuous fragments.

*Fig. 21. Experiment B.7 (Read/Write performance after GC).*
